title: Order of Operations and Expressions
objectives: Apply PEMDAS to evaluate complex expressions
Identify terms, coefficients, and constants in expressions
Combine like terms to simplify expressions

introduction.context: When following a recipe, order matters - you can't frost a cake before baking it! Mathematics has a similar 'recipe' for solving expressions called the order of operations.
introduction.connection: Order of operations appears in calculating costs (tax and discounts), programming formulas, and even in everyday calculations like determining total expenses. We'll master PEMDAS and learn to work with algebraic expressions containing variables.

concepts.title: PEMDAS Order of Operations
concepts.content: The standard order for performing mathematical operations: Parentheses, Exponents, Multiplication and Division (left to right), Addition and Subtraction (left to right). PEMDAS ensures everyone gets the same answer when evaluating expressions.

concepts.title: Algebraic Terms
concepts.content: Parts of an expression separated by addition or subtraction signs. In 3x + 5 - 2y, the terms are 3x, +5, and -2y. Each term can contain numbers, variables, or both.

concepts.title: Distributive Property
concepts.content: Multiplying a number by a sum equals multiplying the number by each addend separately. This property lets us 'distribute' multiplication over addition or subtraction inside parentheses.

commonErrors: Forgetting that multiplication comes before addition
Only multiplying by one term inside parentheses
Substituting the variable before applying distributive property

practice.problem: What operation should be performed first in: 8 + 2 × 3?
practice.explanation: According to PEMDAS, multiplication comes before addition.

hints: Work left to right for same-level operations

practice.explanation: These are like terms. Add the coefficients: 4 + 2 = 6, so 4x + 2x = 6x.
